days.desc: 6 miles total at conversational effort. Let pace follow recovery and conditions; do not force a fixed 9:30 pace. Strides are smooth, not sprints, and stay inside the daily mileage. Strength A after Tuesday: split squat 6–8/side, push-up 6–12, single-leg glute bridge 8–12/side, straight-knee calf raise 10–15/side, side plank 20–30 sec/side. One set for the first two full weeks, then two sets; finish each with 2–3 good reps left. Add backpack/dumbbell load when the top of the range is smooth. Do not lift to failure or chase soreness.

Use the planned workout only with no pain, normal easy-running effort and recovery, and two consistent preceding weeks. Otherwise complete the day easy or follow a recovery reduction. Goal-pace blocks are controlled practice, never a requirement to hold an unsustainable pace. Strength B after Thursday: row or assisted pull-up 6–12, dead bug 6–8/side, side plank 20–30 sec/side. Two controlled sets. On easy Thursdays only, add one or two sets of step-up 6–8/side, hamstring bridge walkout 4–6, and bent-knee calf raise 10–15/side. On quality Thursdays skip the extra lower-body work. In taper, reduce to one light set; no hard leg lifting in race week.

days.desc: Goal is 3:40 only if later training supports it. Choose race pace from your January fitness review. Start conservatively, use practiced fueling, and adjust for conditions. No new shoes, supplements or fueling on race day.

strength.A: Strength A after Tuesday: split squat 6–8/side, push-up 6–12, single-leg glute bridge 8–12/side, straight-knee calf raise 10–15/side, side plank 20–30 sec/side. On easy Thursdays only, add one or two sets of step-up 6–8/side, hamstring bridge walkout 4–6, and bent-knee calf raise 10–15/side. On quality Thursdays skip the extra lower-body work. progressionRule: Advance only after two weeks at >=85% of the adjusted mileage target, at least four run days in each, and low soreness/fatigue with no pain. Otherwise repeat the last completed load and make quality easy. The fifth run adds easy frequency, not catch-up mileage. Do not compress five run days into fewer days. Keep one quality workout per week; in a long-run goal-pace week, Thursday stays easy.
qualityRule: Every faster workout includes easy warm-up and cool-down inside the stated daily distance. Use the planned workout only with no pain, normal easy-running effort and recovery, and two consistent preceding weeks. Otherwise complete the day easy or follow a recovery reduction. Goal-pace blocks are controlled practice, never a requirement to hold an unsustainable pace.

checkpoints.title: Controlled 20-minute benchmark
checkpoints.review: Run the scheduled 20 minutes at a controlled hard effort, not an all-out time trial. Record average pace, effort, and next-day recovery. Use this to set current tempo effort; do not infer a marathon prediction from it.

checkpoints.title: 3:40 readiness review
checkpoints.review: Review consistency, recovery, the January 2 long run, and how 8:23–8:35 blocks felt. Keep 3:40 as the A goal only if the pace is controlled and endurance is progressing. Difficulty at goal pace is a reason to adjust the race target, not force faster easy runs.
